questions.text:
Consider a matrix P whose only eigenvectors are the multiples of [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 4 \end{bmatrix}[/latex].
Consider the following statements.
(I) P does not have an inverse
(II) P has a repeated eigenvalue
(III) P cannot be diagonalized
Which one of the following options is correct?
questions.solution:
A 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 matrix with only one independent eigenvector must have a repeated eigenvalue (II), and without 2 independent eigenvectors it cannot be diagonalized (III). The repeated eigenvalue can be any number, including a non-zero one, and then P is invertible; so I is not necessarily true.

Answer: Only II and III are necessarily true

options: Only I and III are necessarily true
Only I and II are necessarily true
Only II and III are necessarily true

questions.text:
Let N be the set of natural numbers. Consider the following sets.
P: Set of Rational numbers (positive and negative)
Q: Set of functions from {0, 1} to N
R: Set of functions from N to {0, 1}
S: Set of finite subsets of N.
Which of the sets above are countable?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- P (rationals): countable True
- Q (functions {0, 1} [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] N): pairs of natural numbers, N [latex]\times[/latex] N [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] countable True
- R (functions N [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {0, 1}): infinite binary sequences, like subsets of N [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] uncountable False
- S (finite subsets of N): countable union of countable sets [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] countable True

Answer: P, Q and S only

questions.text:
Consider the first-order logic sentence
[latex]\varphi \equiv \exists s\exists t\exists u\forall v\forall w\forall x\forall y\varphi (s,t,u,v,w,x,y)[/latex]
where [latex]\varphi (s,t,u,v,w,x,y)[/latex] is a quantifier-free first-order logic formula using only predicate symbols, and possibly equality, but no function symbols. Suppose [latex]\varphi [/latex] has a model with a universe containing 7 elements. Which one of the following statements is necessarily true?
questions.solution:
The formula has the form [latex]\exists s\,\exists t\,\exists u\,\forall\ldots[/latex] with no function symbols. Take any model and keep only the three elements chosen for s, t, u: universally quantified statements remain true on a subset, so this smaller structure (at most 3 elements) is still a model.

Answer: There exists at least one model with universe of size at most 3

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: There exists at least one model of [latex]\varphi[/latex] with universe of size less than or equal to 3.
There exists no model of [latex]\varphi[/latex] with universe of size less than or equal to 3.
There exists no model of [latex]\varphi[/latex] with universe of size greater than 7.
Every model of [latex]\varphi[/latex] has a universe of size equal to 7.

questions.text:
Let G be a simple undirected graph. Let TD be a depth first search tree of G. Let TB be a breadth first search tree of G. Consider the following statements.

(I) No edge of G is a cross edge with respect to TD. (A cross edge in G is between two nodes neither of which is an ancestor of the other in TD.)
(II) For every edge (u,v) of G, if u is at depth i and v is at depth j in TB, then |i-j|=1.

Which of the statements above must necessarily be true?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- (I): in DFS of an undirected graph, every non-tree edge joins a vertex to its ancestor (back edge); cross edges cannot occur True
- (II): in BFS, an edge can join two vertices at the same depth (e.g. a triangle), so |i [latex]-[/latex] j| can be 0 False

Answer: I only
